sourceHtml:
Terrence O'Brien

is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Suno is facing yet another pair of lawsuits. A group of rights holders of Elvis Presley’s music and the publisher of some of Eminem‘s biggest records are suing the AI music company, claiming it illegally generates music and lyrics that mimic those artists. The lawyers in the Presley suit claim that Suno has violated Tennessee’s Ensuring Likeness Voice and Image Security (ELVIS) Act, which makes it illegal for an AI company to clone a singer’s voice.

In the suit, lawyers representing Presley’s rights holders argue that “Suno has mechanically encoded itself with artists’ identities, hard-work, creativity, and time, and harnessed them all for a consistent conveyor belt of
cold hard cash.“ These suits closely mirror one filed by Jason Isbell and others in September, which claimed Suno created imitations of the plaintiffs but did not claim copyright infringement directly.

Later in the complaint, the lawyers write that “Suno’s ravenous race to the bottom aims to make human creativity obsolete, coldly replicating without a license in seconds what takes years to learn, struggle with, maintain, and endlessly attempt to make better and perfect.”

Suno spokesperson Cat McCormack told The Verge that, “Suno exists to help people create new, original music, not to trade on anyone’s name or likeness, and we prohibit any unauthorized use of an artist’s work. To protect against this, we do not allow prompts for specific artists’ names and songs and work with third-party providers to screen uploaded audio files and lyrics for potential misuse. We are always working to strengthen our guardrails and we will continue to add new safeguards that protect artists and our users.”

This adds to the pile of lawsuits Suno is currently facing from Sony, UMG, Isbell, Reservoir Media, and more.

translation.html:
Terrence O'Brien

是 The Verge 的周末编辑。他报道科技行业已有 18 年多，对合成器也颇有了解。

Suno 又面临两起诉讼。Elvis Presley 音乐的一批权利持有人，以及 Eminem 一些最热门唱片的出版商，正在起诉这家 AI 音乐公司，指控它非法生成模仿这些艺术家的音乐和歌词。Presley 一案的律师声称，Suno 违反了田纳西州的《肖像、声音与影像安全保障（ELVIS）法案》，该法案规定，AI 公司克隆歌手声音属于违法行为。

在诉讼中，代表 Presley 音乐权利持有人的律师辩称，“Suno 以机械方式将艺术家们的身份、辛勤劳动、创造力和时间编码到自身之中，再利用这一切，让流水线源源不断地产出
真金白银。”这些诉讼与 Jason Isbell 等人于 9 月提起的一起诉讼十分相似，后者指控 Suno 制作了模仿原告的作品，但并未直接提出侵犯版权的指控。

在起诉书后文中，律师们写道：“Suno 贪婪地竞相逐底，意在让人类创造力变得过时，将人们需要多年学习、艰苦摸索、持续维系，并不断尝试改进和完善的成果，在未经许可的情况下于几秒内冷冰冰地复制出来。”

Suno 发言人 Cat McCormack 告诉 The Verge：“Suno 的存在是为了帮助人们创作全新的原创音乐，而非利用任何人的姓名或肖像牟利，我们禁止任何未经授权使用艺术家作品的行为。为防范此类情况，我们不允许使用包含特定艺术家姓名和歌曲名称的提示词，并与第三方服务商合作，筛查上传的音频文件和歌词中可能存在的滥用行为。我们一直在努力加强防护措施，并将继续增加新的保障措施，保护艺术家和我们的用户。”

这又给 Suno 目前面临的一连串诉讼添了两起，现有起诉方包括索尼、环球音乐集团（UMG）、Isbell、Reservoir Media 等。
